title: Beyond Affordable Housing: Integrating Civic Infrastructure in US Mixed-Use Developments
text:
Beyond Affordable Housing: Integrating Civic Infrastructure in US Mixed-Use Developments

For much of the twentieth century, affordable housing in the United States was conceived as a distinct residential category, shaped by financing structures and development practices that separated housing for lower-income residents from the broader civic and commercial functions of the city. Federal housing legislation and subsequent urban renewal policies contributed to the construction of large residential developments that were frequently financed and managed independently of surrounding urban infrastructure. The consequences of this approach, including concentrated poverty, deteriorating buildings, unequal access to services, and the eventual demolition of prominent public housing projects, are extensively documented.

title: KOI Restaurant / SOA Architekti
text:
KOI Restaurant / SOA Architekti

The restaurant in Košice occupies a corner building in the historic city centre, in a space that previously housed a clothing or furniture store. The business is run by a father and son. The father brings personal experience, a strong sense of family tradition, and an openness to blending diverse culinary influences into the concept. The son contributes a contemporary gastronomic approach, an understanding of a younger audience, and the energy of an urban venue designed not only for dining but for all-day social life.

title: Konya Square Houses and Bicycle Museum Extension / Yalin Architectural Design
text:
Konya Square Houses and Bicycle Museum Extension / Yalin Architectural Design

Konya Square Houses consists of 13 reinforced-concrete buildings constructed in 2005, drawing on the traditional Konya houses and neighborhood fabric that existed on the site until 1955. Over the years, the complex accommodated various non-governmental organizations and municipal departments.

title: DamDam House / Studio SMA + Ground Architects
text:
DamDam House / Studio SMA + Ground Architects

DamDam is a compact house for a couple, their twins, and two cats, designed with solid exterior walls to ensure privacy on a small site surrounded by taller buildings. Working within the constraints of the parking layout, the functions of each floor were carefully separated, and the circulation was precisely planned to maximize the usability of the interior spaces.

title: Virtual Studio at the Cidade das TIC, A Coruña Arms Factory / Diaz y Diaz Architects
text:
Virtual Studio at the Cidade das TIC, A Coruña Arms Factory / Diaz y Diaz Architects

In the former Weapons Factory of A Coruña, the Virtual Studio translates an essential duality into architecture: a hermetic box designed to create digital worlds versus an open volume that dialogues with the landscape and the industrial memory of the site.

title: Alaska Airlines Flagship Lounge / Graham Baba Architects
text:
Alaska Airlines Flagship Lounge / Graham Baba Architects

At the Alaska Airlines Flagship Lounge in SeaTac International Airport, the door is always open. Travelers seek lounges as an escape from the anxiety, noise, and commotion of the concourse. Traditionally, airport lounges catered to this desire by emphasizing exclusivity: sleek, business-oriented safe havens that prioritized the needs of a privileged swath of travelers. Alaska Airlines sought to transform the lounge typology by providing a warm, welcoming space where all guests could find refuge – to relax, work, refuel and connect – a home-away-from-home with a sense of place deeply rooted in the Pacific Northwest. Programmatically, the lounge is conceived in four zones: Come In, an approachable entry; Help Yourself, a casual bistro; Take a Breath, a haven for peaceful relaxation; and Cut Loose, a cozy bar atmosphere. Lightly separated with an array of oak and twisted metal screens, the spaces flow together.

title: Brooklin Apartment / Küster Brizola Arquitetos
text:
Brooklin Apartment / Küster Brizola Arquitetos

Designed by the firm Küster Brizola Arquitetos, this 200-square-meter apartment in Brooklin, São Paulo, turns the traditional checkerboard floor into the main protagonist of the project, developed for a couple with two children. The residence was born from the desire to create a home focused on gathering, hosting friends and family, and building cherished memories, reinterpreting the classic pattern as the organizing element of the social area and the apartment's identity.

title: Sunnyside Studios / Gluck+
text:
Sunnyside Studios / Gluck+

Sunnyside Studios rethinks the soundstage typology for a city where land can't spread horizontally. Studio campuses are typically conceived as backlots: individual soundstage boxes, each its own building, linked by golf carts and an interior street network. That model depends on land New York City doesn't have. The key concept driving the project was to compress everything a campus needs — stages, production support, loading, parking, catering, crew, and talent onto a single urban block without losing the operational logic that makes a campus work.

title: Alonakia House / React Architects
text:
Alonakia House / React Architects

Situated on a steep west-facing slope in Antiparos, the house overlooks the open Aegean and the long horizon of the setting sun. Its design begins with the condition of the site: a rugged terrain in which building is inseparable from the act of shaping the ground. Instead of introducing a singular object onto the hillside, the project is conceived as a continuation of the existing topography, translating the characteristics of the Cycladic landscape into a contemporary dwelling.

title: Planned Overflow: How Singapore Balances Floods, Canals, and Public Space
text:
Planned Overflow: How Singapore Balances Floods, Canals, and Public Space

At Bishan–Ang Mo Kio Park in Singapore, a river does not occupy a fixed boundary. Under ordinary conditions, water moves through a naturalized channel bordered by grass, planting, and paths that bring visitors close to the river. During heavy rainfall, water spreads into the surrounding park, which is designed to accommodate flows beyond the capacity of the narrower channel. What appears to be a public landscape is also working infrastructure. Singapore's approach retains drainage engineering while assigning a wider role to the land around it.

title: Simple Structures, Multiple Uses: Rethinking the Schoolyard and Its Canopy / 127af
text:
Simple Structures, Multiple Uses: Rethinking the Schoolyard and Its Canopy / 127af

At Paul Bert Elementary School in Itteville, south of Paris, the transformation of an asphalt schoolyard into a planted landscape and the construction of a new canopy explore how simple materials and construction techniques can create a cooler, more inclusive environment for children.

title: Rancho del Abuelo / Mendiola Arregui
text:
Rancho del Abuelo / Mendiola Arregui

Rancho del Abuelo is an equestrian complex located in Jalisco, on the outskirts of Guadalajara. Its program coordinates spaces dedicated to the sheltering and care of horses with others designed for resting, gathering, and contemplation, establishing different ways of living and engaging with the landscape and equestrian life.

title: House in Vinhedo / Apiacás Arquitetos
text:
House in Vinhedo / Apiacás Arquitetos

The flat terrain with generous dimensions, intended for a residence with a maximum area of 250 m², motivated us to position it in a way to maximize the interface between the covered program and the external areas. The resulting distribution follows a logic already tested in other residential projects by the office, where the circulation between the rooms is configured as covered passages, yet open laterally — without frames or masonry — to extend the experience between the interior and exterior.

title: Casa Neblina  / Red Arquitectos
text:
Casa Neblina / Red Arquitectos

Enclavada entre huertas y palmares de El Pescadero, Casa Neblina es un monolito beige que emerge de la bruma salina del amanecer como una piedra más del paisaje del desierto.

title: Hotel MS Collection Arouca / MiMool Arquitectura & Design de Interiores
text:
Hotel MS Collection Arouca / MiMool Arquitectura & Design de Interiores

The rehabilitation of the former Monastery of Santa Maria de Arouca, classified as a National Monument since 1910, proposes the transformation of a significant part of the monastic complex into a five-star hotel, integrated into the REVIVE program. Rather than a mere functional adaptation, the project stands as an exercise in historical continuity, where architecture, memory, and landscape articulate into a new narrative of use and permanence.

title: The Turquoise House / SUPRBLK Studio
text:
The Turquoise House / SUPRBLK Studio

The Turquoise House fits a family home, architecture studioand independent apartment onto a narrow Halifax lot, using two gabled volumes and a series of courtyards to create density without sacrificing light, privacy or connection to the outdoors.

title: AEME Building / Paz Arquitectura
text:
AEME Building / Paz Arquitectura

AEME is a building located in Guatemala City. It has an open floor plan on the first floor dedicated to commercial use and restaurants, a second floor that combines commerce and offices, and three floors exclusively dedicated to offices. The first floor is connected to the street through a double-height entrance with the purpose of emphasizing the opening towards a friendly urban use, with an aim to allow the first floor to be interpreted as an extension of the public space.

title: Rotiers - Renovation of 46 housing units in Brussels  / MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism
text:
Rotiers - Renovation of 46 housing units in Brussels / MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism

The Rotiers project aims to give a renewed architectural identity to a 1960s social housing building while preserving the qualities of its setting. Located at the edge of the Sonian Forest and surrounded by mature trees, the building is renovated in close relation to its landscape. The intervention addresses several scales, from the building's integration into the neighborhood to the everyday experience of residents and neighbors, with particular attention to the dwellings, shared outdoor spaces, and entrances.

title: Villa Moderne: In Search of Hong Kong Modern Homes
text:
Villa Moderne: In Search of Hong Kong Modern Homes

Recreating the modern villas that shaped Hong Kong from the 1930s to the 1980s, this book offers a glimpse into the architecture and lifestyles of high society, tracing how these homes helped shape the city’s neighbourhoods and urban history.

Hong Kong’s modern villas reveal a side of the city rarely seen in its skyline. From the 1930s onwards, they appeared on hillsides, beside coastal roads and in newly planned suburbs, reflecting changing ideas of what a modern home could be.

text:
With and Without Walls: The Southern California Institute of Architecture in the 1970s and 1980s

The institutional history, With and Without Walls, reveals the origins and progress of the influential Southern California Institute of Architecture (SCI-Arc) through the 1970s and 1980s.
